title: Architecture styles (boxology family tree)
literature: Shaw & Garlan 'Software Architecture: Perspectives'; Garlan & Shaw 'Intro to Software Architecture' boxology; Taylor, Medvidovic & Dashofy style taxonomy; Fielding REST; dataflow/call-return/repository/layered/event families.

members.name: Actor-Based Architecture
members.what: Organizes the whole system as actors that own their state and interact only via asynchronous messages processed run-to-completion from per-actor mailboxes.

members.name: Adaptive Object Model
members.what: Represents classes, attributes and rules as runtime data (metadata) interpreted by a generic engine, so the domain model is changed by users, not by code.

members.name: Batch Sequential
members.what: A degenerate data-flow organization in which each processing step runs to completion on the entire data set before passing the complete result to the next step.

members.name: Blackboard
members.what: Independent specialized knowledge sources cooperate by reading and writing partial solutions on a shared data structure (the blackboard) under a control component's opportunistic scheduling.

members.name: Blockchain
members.what: A peer-to-peer system maintains a replicated append-only ledger of Merkle-chained blocks agreed by a consensus mechanism.

members.name: Broker
members.what: Structures a distributed system around an intermediary component that coordinates remote service invocations - locating servers, marshalling requests/replies, and reporting errors - so clients and servers stay decoupled from location and tr

members.name: C2
members.what: A layered, message-based style in which components communicate only through explicit connectors via asynchronous notifications (downward) and requests (upward), under a strict substrate-independence rule: a component may know services above

members.name: Channel Architecture
members.what: Organizing the system as one or more end-to-end channels, each a sequential chain of data transformations from sensing to actuation, so that redundancy and safety measures can be applied per-channel.

members.name: Clean Architecture
members.what: Concentric layers (entities, use cases, interface adapters, frameworks) with all source dependencies pointing inward toward policy.

members.name: Client-Server
members.what: Server components provide services at known locations while client components initiate requests for them, typically via remote procedure call or request/response protocols, with the server unaware of client identities in advance.

members.name: Code-on-Demand
members.what: A mobile-code style in which a client that has the data and processing resources requests executable code (know-how) from a remote server and runs it locally, as with scripts delivered to a browser.

members.name: Component-Based Architecture
members.what: Structures the whole system as replaceable components with explicit provided/required interfaces (ROOM: capsules with ports and protocols).

members.name: Data-Parallel Architecture
members.what: The same program is applied concurrently across partitions of a large regular data set, each unit of execution running identical code over its own data slice (SPMD / geometric decomposition).

members.name: Dataflow Architecture
members.what: Organizes the whole system around the availability and movement of data through transforming nodes rather than control flow.

members.name: Distributed Commit Log
members.what: A partitioned, replicated append-only log serves as the system's ordering and integration backbone; producers append, consumers replay at their own pace.

members.name: Distributed Objects
members.what: System functionality is partitioned into objects whose methods can be invoked across process and machine boundaries through proxies and an object request broker, preserving OO interfaces over the network.

members.name: Distributed Processes
members.what: The system is a set of independent processes, typically on multiple processors, interacting by message passing under some topological organization (ring, star, arbitrary graph).

members.name: Event-Based Implicit Invocation
members.what: Components announce (broadcast) events instead of invoking procedures directly; the system implicitly invokes every procedure registered as interested in that event.

members.name: Event-Driven Architecture
members.what: The system is organized around the production, detection, and asynchronous reaction to events, with components emitting and subscribing to event notifications through a mediator or broker rather than calling each other directly.

members.name: Event Sourcing (architecture style)
aka: event store as system of record
members.what: System-level persistence strategy where the event log is the source of truth for whole services and downstream projections/read models are derived from it.

members.name: Event-Triggered Architecture
members.what: System-level organization in which communication and task activation are initiated by the occurrence of significant events (interrupts, message arrivals) rather than by a global clock; Kopetz names it as the counterpoint to time-triggered c

members.name: File Transfer
members.what: Applications integrate by one producing files of shared data and others consuming them, with an agreed format and transfer/processing cadence.

members.name: Function-Queue-Scheduling Architecture
members.what: A system structure in which interrupts enqueue pointers to task functions and the main loop dequeues and runs them to completion, allowing priority ordering of the queue without a preemptive kernel.

members.name: Hexagonal Architecture
members.what: Application core exposes technology-neutral ports; adapters translate between each external actor (UI, DB, tests, other systems) and the ports.

members.name: Interpreter (Architectural Style)
members.what: The system is organized as a virtual machine: an interpretation engine, the pseudo-program it executes, and the engine's and program's state, closing the gap between the execution platform and the desired semantics.

members.name: Kappa Architecture
members.what: Everything is a stream: a single stream-processing pipeline over a replayable log serves both real-time and reprocessing needs, eliminating the separate batch layer.

members.name: Lambda Architecture
members.what: Data system split into a batch layer (immutable master dataset, recomputed views), a speed layer (incremental real-time views), and a serving layer merging both.

members.name: Layers
members.what: Structures a whole system as a hierarchy of abstraction levels in which each layer offers services to the layer above and uses only the layer(s) below.

members.name: LMAX Architecture
aka: business logic processor with input/output disruptors
members.what: A single-threaded in-memory business logic processor is fed and drained by ring-buffer (Disruptor) pipelines, with event sourcing for durability.

members.name: Main Program and Subroutines
members.what: A single main program drives the system by calling a hierarchy of subroutines, with control returning up the call tree after each call.

members.name: MapReduce
members.what: Batch computation structured as a parallel map phase over partitioned input, a shuffle, and a reduce phase, scheduled across a cluster by a framework.

members.name: Message Bus
members.what: A shared messaging backbone - common channels, a common data model, and a common command set - that all applications plug into to interoperate, joining or leaving without affecting the others.

members.name: Messaging
members.what: Applications integrate by exchanging discrete asynchronous messages over channels provided by a messaging infrastructure, decoupling senders from receivers in time and availability.

members.name: Micro Frontends
members.what: Frontend decomposed into independently built and deployed UI fragments owned end-to-end by the teams owning the corresponding backend services.

members.name: Microkernel
members.what: Separates a minimal functional core (fundamental services, communication, extension management) from extended functionality delivered as internal/external servers or plug-ins loaded onto the core.

members.name: Microservices
members.what: Suite of small, independently deployable services, each owning its data, communicating over lightweight network mechanisms, organized around business capabilities.

members.name: Mobile Agent
members.what: A mobile-code style in which an entire computational unit - code, execution state, and data - migrates itself from site to site, resuming execution at each destination.

members.name: Modular Monolith
members.what: Single deployable unit whose interior is decomposed into strictly encapsulated modules with enforced boundaries.

members.name: Monolithic Architecture
members.what: The whole application is built and deployed as a single deployable unit.

members.name: N-Tier Client-Server
members.what: Client-server generalized to a chain of tiers (e.g. presentation, business logic, data management), each acting as server to the tier before it and client of the tier after it, deployable on separate machines.

members.name: Object-Oriented Organization
members.what: The system is organized as a collection of abstract-data-type instances (objects) that hide their representations and interact by invoking each other's operations.

members.name: Peer-to-Peer
members.what: Networked components (peers) act as both clients and servers of one another, discovering and exchanging services directly without a distinguished central server.

members.name: Pipes and Filters
members.what: Organizes a processing system as a chain of independent filter components connected by pipes that carry a data stream from source to sink.

members.name: Process Control (Feedback Control Loop)
members.what: The system is organized around a control loop: a controller reads process variables from sensors, compares them to set points, and adjusts manipulated variables to keep a physical or continuing process on target.

members.name: Protocol Layering
members.what: Structures communication software as a stack of protocol layers, each providing services to the layer above and encapsulating its PDU inside the layer below.

members.name: Publish-Subscribe (Architectural Style)
members.what: Publishers emit messages classified by topic or content to an intermediary event service, which delivers them to all components that have subscribed, so producers and consumers never address each other.

members.name: Remote Evaluation
members.what: A mobile-code style in which a component that has the know-how sends code to a remote site that has the resources and data, where it executes and returns results.

members.name: Remote Procedure Invocation
members.what: Applications integrate by exposing procedures/services that other applications invoke synchronously over the network to exchange data and trigger behavior.

members.name: Repository (Shared Data) Style
members.what: A central data structure represents the system state while a collection of independent components operate on it, coordinating only through the shared store.

members.name: REST (Representational State Transfer)
members.what: A hybrid network-based style constraining client-server interaction to be stateless, cacheable, layered, and mediated by a uniform interface over resources identified by URIs and manipulated via exchanged representations, optionally extende

members.name: RTOS-Based Architecture
members.what: A whole-system structure in which the application is decomposed into prioritized, preemptively scheduled RTOS tasks communicating through kernel objects (queues, semaphores, events), with response times set by priority rather than loop posi

members.name: Rule-Based System
members.what: An interpreter specialization in which a rule engine (inference/interpretation engine) selects and fires condition-action rules from a knowledge base against working memory.

members.name: SEDA (Staged Event-Driven Architecture)
members.what: Service structured as a network of event-driven stages connected by explicit queues, each stage with its own thread pool and admission control.

members.name: Sense-Compute-Control
members.what: An embedded-systems organization structured as a repeating loop of sensor reading, computation over the sensed values plus internal state, and actuator commands controlling the environment.

members.name: Service-Based Architecture
members.what: Small number of coarse-grained, separately deployed domain services sharing a single database, typically fronted by one UI.

members.name: Service-Oriented Architecture
members.what: Enterprise organized as coarse-grained reusable business/enterprise services coordinated through a mediating integration layer (often an ESB/orchestrator).

members.name: Shared Database
members.what: Multiple applications integrate by reading and writing the same database schema, making one store the single point of data agreement.

members.name: Shared-Nothing Architecture
members.what: Nodes own disjoint partitions of data and memory and coordinate only by messages; no shared disk or shared memory.

members.name: Space-Based Architecture
members.what: Processing units with replicated in-memory data grids, synchronized asynchronously to persistent storage, so the database is out of the request path.

members.name: State Transition System (Architectural Organization)
members.what: A whole reactive system is organized as a set of states plus named transitions that move the system between them, making the state machine the top-level structure rather than an internal mechanism.

members.name: Streaming Dataflow Architecture
members.what: Structures data processing as a long-running dataflow graph over unbounded streams with windowing, watermarks and triggers.

members.name: Subsumption Architecture
members.what: Layers of behavior-producing modules run concurrently, with higher layers subsuming (suppressing/overriding) the outputs of lower ones instead of a central planner.

members.name: Superloop Architecture
members.what: A whole-system structure with no operating system: one endless main loop polls and services every task in turn, optionally with interrupts as the foreground layer feeding flags/buffers to the background loop.

members.name: Time-Triggered Architecture
members.what: System-level organization in which all communication and computation are driven by the progression of a fault-tolerant global time base, with statically planned activation instants known a priori at all nodes.

members.name: Virtual Machine (architectural style)
members.what: Builds the system atop an abstract machine whose instruction set is interpreted, decoupling applications from the physical platform.

members.name: Zero Trust Architecture
members.what: A security architecture in which no implicit trust is granted by network location; every access to a resource is individually authenticated and authorized per session via policy decision/enforcement points.
